question: One card is lost from a well-shuffled deck of $52$ playing cards. From the remaining deck, two cards are drawn successively without replacement and both are found to be face cards. Determine the probability that the lost card was a face card.
explanation:
Given Information
A standard deck contains $12$ face cards and $40$ non-face cards. Let $E_1$ be the event that the lost card is a face card and $E_2$ the event that the lost card is a non-face card. Let $A$ denote the event that the two cards drawn from the remaining deck are both face cards. Then
$$P(E_1)=\frac{12}{52},\qquad P(E_2)=\frac{40}{52}.$$
If a face card was lost, $11$ face cards remain among $51$ cards, so
$$P(A|E_1)=\frac{11}{51}\times\frac{10}{50}.$$
If a non-face card was lost, all $12$ face cards remain, so
$$P(A|E_2)=\frac{12}{51}\times\frac{11}{50}.$$

Applying Total Probability and Bayes’ Theorem
The theorem of total probability gives
$$P(A)=P(E_1)P(A|E_1)+P(E_2)P(A|E_2).$$
Therefore, by Bayes’ theorem,
$$P(E_1|A)=\frac{P(E_1)P(A|E_1)}{P(E_1)P(A|E_1)+P(E_2)P(A|E_2)}.$$
Substituting the values,
$$P(E_1|A)=\frac{\frac{12}{52}\times\frac{11}{51}\times\frac{10}{50}}{\frac{12}{52}\times\frac{11}{51}\times\frac{10}{50}+\frac{40}{52}\times\frac{12}{51}\times\frac{11}{50}}.$$
Common factors cancel, giving
$$P(E_1|A)=\frac{12\times10}{12\times10+40\times12}=\frac{120}{600}=\frac{1}{5}.$$

Final Result
Hence, the probability that the lost card was a face card is $\frac{1}{5}$.
